name: Insurrectionary anarchism
summary: Insurrectionary anarchism holds that the state and capitalism will not disappear on their own and must be attacked now, through small, informal, self-managed affinity groups rather than parties, unions or federations. It treats conflict with those in power as permanent, refuses negotiation, mediation and compromise, and regards illegal and violent direct action as legitimate means. It rejects work, democracy, law and organised religion as mechanisms of domination, and sees insurrections as the daily building blocks of social revolution.
scope: The Italian-rooted insurrectionist tendency of Alfredo Bonanno (Armed Joy, 1977; The Insurrectional Project, 1998), the 'Some Notes on Insurrectionary Anarchism' theses, and precursors such as Luigi Galleani and Marcus Graham, as summarised on Wikipedia. Excludes organised anarcho-syndicalism, platformism and mainstream social anarchism; the anarcho-primitivist offshoot is treated as a separate strand, and many answers on topics the texts never address are low-confidence inferences from anti-state, anti-capitalist principles.

furtherReading.title: Some Notes on Insurrectionary Anarchism
furtherReading.note: A short, readable set of theses on attack, permanent conflict and informal organisation.

furtherReading.title: The Insurrectional Project (Alfredo M. Bonanno)
furtherReading.note: Bonanno's 1998 essay on capitalism's restructuring and insurrectional organisation.

furtherReading.title: Armed Joy (Alfredo M. Bonanno)
furtherReading.note: The 1977 text that made the case for joyful attack and a critique of work.

keyFigures.name: Alfredo Maria Bonanno
keyFigures.role: Main theorist of contemporary insurrectionary anarchism and author of Armed Joy.

keyFigures.name: Luigi Galleani
keyFigures.role: Early advocate of insurrectionism and propaganda of the deed in the United States.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Insurrectionists do not ask the state for services; they would reject state provision on principle yet favour free access to care, so adherents split and the sources are silent.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Wage-setting bargains within wage labour and the state, which insurrectionists regard as reformist mediation; inferred from their refusal of negotiation and compromise.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: Capitalism and commodity logic are targets of attack, and Bonanno wants exchange freed from abstract value.

public-ownership.rationale: State ownership strengthens the state, which they seek to destroy, and nationalised industry is still capital.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Asking the state to redistribute is delegating emancipation to institutions; they would rather expropriate directly.

unions-good.rationale: Unions are called corrupted from the start and an integration device for capital and state.

property-fundamental.rationale: Bonanno says wealth should be seized and used, and treats law and property as capital's mythology.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Regulation is state mediation that leaves capital intact; inferred from refusal of reform through institutions.

cut-welfare.rationale: They despise the welfare state as pacification, but do not defend benefits as such; inferred, leaning against cuts that hurt the exploited.

worker-ownership.rationale: They favour self-organisation of producers but reject formal workplace organisations and the idealisation of production, so only weak support.

surveillance-ok.rationale: Anti-state and illegalist, they treat surveillance as a counter-insurgency tool to be evaded and attacked.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Not a stated theme, but anti-prohibition and hostile to state policing of individual choice is the usual anarchist view; inferred.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: They reject state censorship and legal mediation, though many would respond to bigots by direct confrontation; inferred.

strong-leader.rationale: Opposed to all authority and informal groups avoid leaders; Bonanno calls for eliminating all power.

limit-guns.rationale: Armed attack is central, and they would not look to the state to restrict arms; the issue itself is unaddressed.

empower-police-military.rationale: Bonanno holds that it is better to shoot policemen, and police and army are instruments of the state they seek to destroy.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Not discussed in sources; anti-work and anti-state stance suggests tolerance of consenting choices, but views vary.

decide-locally.rationale: They favour self-managed autonomous struggle, but not formal local government which is still democratic management.

rehabilitation.rationale: They reject prison itself; Bonanno predicts asylums replacing prisons, a rehabilitation-style control they criticise.

traditional-family.rationale: Hostile to inherited social roles and Christian morality; the family is not directly discussed, so inferred.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: Marriage as a state institution is rejected, so they would not campaign for legalisation, but have no objection to the lives it protects.

abortion-legal.rationale: Not addressed in sources; bodily autonomy and anti-state outlook suggest support for choice, inferred.

more-religion-public.rationale: Anticlericalism is a core principle, and Bonanno ties the work ethic to Christian sacrifice.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: They oppose racism but refuse state remedies and identity politics that impose roles; adherents split.

gender-social-construct.rationale: They reject identity and imposed social roles, so a constructionist view fits, though the sources do not say it.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: They oppose nationalism, which Bonanno sees as dangerous, and reject state-imposed tradition.

gradual-change.rationale: Waiting only teaches waiting; they reject gradualism and respect for institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: Anti-state and against borders; Bonanno condemns the fear of the foreigner.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: International bodies are state and capital structures they oppose.

free-trade.rationale: Bonanno describes the global coordination of capital as domination, and free trade is its mechanism.

nation-first.rationale: Nationalism is rejected as dangerous, and states generally are targets.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: State military action is opposed whatever its stated purpose.

open-borders.rationale: Opposed to states, so to borders; adherents regard border controls as state violence.

limit-growth.rationale: Bonanno criticises capital's ecological restructuring but not growth as such; sources do not settle it.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: They distrust state-led ecological management as capitalist restructuring, though they want polluters attacked.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: Bonanno says new technologies will always be instruments of death, and Graham criticised technology.

expand-nuclear.rationale: Large technological systems under state or capital are opposed; inferred from hostility to technology.

revolution-justified.rationale: Revolution is the constant point of reference and insurrection is its step.

experts-over-public.rationale: They reject hierarchical authority, and Bonanno condemns anyone claiming to hold the truth.

central-planning.rationale: Opposed to vanguard and state structures, and they reject the state as organiser of production.

socialized-markets.rationale: Markets and public ownership both leave commodity exchange and the state intact; they favour direct non-commodity circulation.

land-value-tax.rationale: A tax is a state mechanism, not an anarchist programme; inferred.

tax-inheritance.rationale: They want direct expropriation, not state taxation; inferred.

basic-income.rationale: A state payment is institutional integration, though recipients may take it; inferred.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: Protecting national industry serves states and capital, and nationalism is rejected.

state-directs-investment.rationale: State direction of capital is capitalist restructuring they oppose.

widespread-small-property.rationale: They oppose property as such; small owners are less harmful but still a property system.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: Bonanno proposes a non-work aesthetic and exchange free of abstract value; the revolution is negation of labour.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: Abolition is acceptable to them, but leaving money to the market is not their aim.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: State-recognised bodies are the integration of workers into capital and state that they attack.

one-party-rule.rationale: Opposed to parties and all power.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: Complete elimination of all power is the goal.

democracy-best.rationale: Bonanno calls elections and referenda fictitious and democratic management a domination tool.

direct-votes.rationale: Votes on laws still presuppose the state and binding majorities; they prefer autonomous action.

workers-councils.rationale: Bonanno favours self-organisation of producers, but they reject permanent bodies and a political power basis.

right-to-secede.rationale: Weakening states is welcome and some adherents link to national liberation, but nationalism is not endorsed.

political-violence-never.rationale: Violence is central rather than a last resort.

war-builds-character.rationale: Bonanno warns armed struggle is often a symbol of death, and they reject state wars.

separate-church-state.rationale: Anticlericalism, but they reject the state itself, so the separation is not their programme.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: Law and religion are both rejected, Bonanno ties Christian ethic to sacrifice.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Courts are theatre serving capital; private versions are no better.

ethnic-nation.rationale: Nationalism is rejected; Bonanno attacks fear of the foreigner.

class-struggle-history.rationale: The exploited are capital's fundamental contradiction and permanent conflict is stressed, though they dislike economic determinism.

equal-outcomes.rationale: They want an end to domination, but reject imposed equality of being; sources do not address.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Some sympathy with autonomous struggles but no authority over land is endorsed; not addressed.

colonial-reparations.rationale: Reparations are claims on states and mediated by them; inferred.

civilizational-union.rationale: Supranational state-building is opposed, and religious integralisms are criticised.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Individual autonomy and freedom from Christian sacrifice are prized, with egoist roots, but not stated as self-interest morality.

duties-before-rights.rationale: Bonanno attacks sacrifice and community morality imposed on individuals.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecology is discussed only as capital's restructuring; some strands are green, others not.

limit-population.rationale: State population control is rejected; inferred.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: Graham called for destroying civilisation and Bonanno sees technology as death, but it is not core for all adherents.

accelerate-technology.rationale: Technological restructuring is capital's strategy and technology is an instrument of death.

human-enhancement.rationale: Distrust of technology outweighs a freedom-of-choice view; inferred.

algorithmic-government.rationale: Technology as control and government alike are rejected.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: Evading surveillance and counter-insurgency is practical to illegal action.

restore-past-order.rationale: They reject established order and are future-directed negation.

results-over-ideology.rationale: They stress principles like refusal of compromise over pragmatism.

direct-action.rationale: Attack and self-organised action replace mediation and parliamentary decree.

means-match-ends.rationale: Prefigurative politics is not a core commitment, and they clashed with prefigurative activists, though they emphasise self-management.

return-to-foraging.rationale: Only the anarcho-primitivist offshoot holds it; mainstream insurrectionists do not.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: The non-work aesthetic and critique of production suggest it, but not stated as such.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Bonanno envisions circulation of goods and use of wealth, communist in outlook; not a worked-out claim.

production-for-use.rationale: Commodity logic must be destroyed and goods used, not accumulated.

profit-exploitation.rationale: The exploited are capitalism's contradiction; profit from ownership is exploitation in anarchist analysis.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: They reject vanguards, parties and any dictatorship.

collective-farming.rationale: They avoid prescribing forms of production and reject imposed collectivism.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: Bonanno describes managed imperialism as part of capital's restructuring.

taxation-theft.rationale: They view the state as illegitimate so its levies are coercion, though they do not argue it as a principle.

harm-principle.rationale: They reject the state's authority to restrict anyone; the principle as stated presumes a legitimate state.

individual-rights-only.rationale: They reject rights as state-granted, not defending individual-only rights.

conscription.rationale: Opposed to armies and state coercion.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Neither voting nor leaving, which is a liberal framing; they attack.

state-as-business.rationale: The state is rejected rather than managed.

positive-liberty.rationale: They want material freedom to act but reject state provision; not addressed.

media-academia-power.rationale: Mass media and spectacle are criticised, but they see capital and the state as the real power.

organic-representation.rationale: Representation of any kind is rejected.

total-state.rationale: Complete elimination of power is the aim.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Oaths binding followers to lords are a hierarchy of power, which Bonanno wants eliminated entirely.

bound-labor.rationale: Unfree labour is the opposite of their critique of work and authority.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: They treat state and law as capital's myths, but have no stated epistemology.

universal-morality.rationale: Bonanno rejects morality as capital's mythology and Christian ethics.

single-common-good.rationale: They reject imposed unity and rational authority over conflicting interests.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: A state for any people is opposed, and nationalism is rejected.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Return rights are tied to state citizenship; adherents oppose nation-states but favour free movement.

revive-national-language.rationale: State language policy and nationalism are rejected.

workplace-democracy.rationale: They favour self-organisation but call democratic management a control form.

school-vouchers.rationale: Not addressed; state schooling in any form is rejected, and vouchers keep a market in education.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is state business of no interest to them.

economic-freedom.rationale: Economic freedom as liberals mean it is capitalism; they reject it.

national-self-determination.rationale: Nationalism is dangerous though it may dismantle large states, so only partial sympathy.

force-without-un.rationale: State military force is opposed whatever the approval.

reason-over-faith.rationale: Bonanno stresses joy and play and also attacks the priest as truth-claimer; mixed.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: Borders and citizenship are state categories rejected by anarchists.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Bonanno rejects the work ethic outright.

class-collaboration.rationale: Permanent conflict and refusal of compromise with class enemies.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Inheritance of culture is not a concern for them, nor is destruction of institutions for its own sake; not addressed.

dominated-front.rationale: They oppose the Western powers but not through state-led fronts.

workers-nation.rationale: Nationalism and trade-union structures alike are rejected.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: Imposed social roles and identity are rejected.

ban-interest.rationale: They oppose state bans and finance alike; no stated position.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Racism and state classification both opposed.

state-class-instrument.rationale: The state serves capital and parties and syndicates integrate struggle into it; they do not have a strictly Marxist view.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Capital's extraction is opposed, though not from a policy stance.

elite-replacement.rationale: Racist conspiracy is contrary to their view; Bonanno condemns fear of the foreigner.

proportional-representation.rationale: Elections are fictitious and they oppose representation altogether.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: Anarcha-feminism overlaps and they oppose domination, but the sources do not discuss it.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: Unions, parties and politicians are called careerists and part of the spectacle.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: State control of reproduction is opposed.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: Courts are theatre of capital, so they do not ask legal accountability, though want police attacked.

night-watchman-state.rationale: Even a minimal state defending property and enforcing justice is a state, and they seek to destroy it.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: They say individuality needs no imposed equality of being, but no hierarchy of worth either; legal rights are state matters.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: All states are domination, but this particular claim is not stated.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: State legal codes of any kind are rejected.

restrict-conversion.rationale: State restriction of belief is opposed, as is clerical power.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: Not discussed; state bans are opposed.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Anticlerical, though they reject state schools themselves.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: The state must not strengthen, and they reject any socialist state.

consent-of-governed.rationale: They see elections as fictions and reject authority however based on consent.

population-transfer.rationale: State coercion and racism both opposed.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: Attack and violence against police, property and capital are central.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: Individuality matters but they emphasise play and community, not competition.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: They oppose state repression of dissent even if they reject parties.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Elimination of all power and domination is Bonanno's goal.

separated-powers.rationale: Not wanting any government to check; all power is rejected.

vanguard-party.rationale: Bonanno opposes vanguards and centralised parties, preferring affinity groups.

priority-to-poor.rationale: They stand with the exploited but through attack, not institutional priorities.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: It is a state programme; not addressed.

restrict-strikes-picketing.rationale: State restriction of direct action is opposed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: The exploited are poor because of capitalism.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: Condemnation of racism and rejection of imposed sameness.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: Offices themselves are rejected; a lottery would still be rule.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State economic management is not their programme, but scarcity is hardly their concern; unaddressed.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: Citizenship is a state creation they reject.

representatives-worker-pay.rationale: They reject representation outright, so wage caps are beside the point.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: Parties and binding discipline are rejected.

head-commands-forces.rationale: No head of state or army.

clerical-rule.rationale: Anticlericalism is a core principle, so rule by religious scholars is rejected.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: They want attack on state and capital, so wars are occasions for revolt; inferred.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: Opposed to morality as capital's mythology and state censorship.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: Elections are fictitious; no rulers are wanted.

recall-officials.rationale: Reforming officials is not their aim; inferred.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: They want armies abolished, not national withdrawal; mild agreement.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: They oppose property as such, but want it seized, not a state edict of ownership.

people-in-arms.rationale: Armed attack is central and nobody should depend on a professional army.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Not addressed; Bonanno mentions the killing of the landscape but is not rural-romantic.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: The sources never discuss educated people as a class, so there is no stated position.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: They reject racism but have no stated cultural relativism.

death-penalty.rationale: They oppose state killing and the courts.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: They reject state schooling but not the content.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Anticlerical and against religious state instruction.

minority-language-support.rationale: State support is not their demand though they oppose language coercion.

religious-exemptions.rationale: They reject law itself, not carving exceptions for religion.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: They reject imposed identity and equality of being, and favour individuality.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: They attack capital's global coordination, so cancellation is welcome, though they ask nothing of states.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: Nationalism may dismantle states but the capitalist system must be attacked.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: Opposed to state restriction of anything.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: State aid is mediation; they favour direct attack and solidarity.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: States, arms and technology of death are rejected.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: Elections fictitious; no head of state.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Central banks are part of capital's coordination; independence is not their issue.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: They do not justify property conditionally; they reject it.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: Bonanno condemns vanguards and idealised production, and anarchists generally hold this view.

precautionary-principle.rationale: Not addressed; state action is distrusted.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: They oppose all states, so annexation is not a legitimacy question.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: They are anticlerical but reject state authority as a solution.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: A symbolic head of state is still an office of power, and they reject all such office.

region-keeps-system.rationale: It is a state arrangement they do not care about.

flat-income-tax.rationale: Taxation is a state matter and not their programme.

character-from-environment.rationale: Social roles shape identity, they hold; no psychology stated.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: No power should stand above anyone; law is part of capital's spectacle.

space-expansion.rationale: Technology and capital projects are rejected.

mixed-constitution.rationale: No constitutions or governments are wanted.

equal-parenting.rationale: Courts are rejected; family law not addressed.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: They distrust states claiming socialism and say revolutionary class disappears into production worship.

land-redistribution.rationale: Expropriation is welcome but redistribution by the state to farmers is not.

refugee-return.rationale: Free movement and opposition to expulsions follow from anti-state views.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: They are anticlerical and oppose state punishment of belief or its abandonment.

women-must-cover.rationale: Opposed to state compulsion and religious authority.

common-currency.rationale: Currency is a tool of capital; unions of states are still states.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: They reject nationalism and state-recognised bodies.

rights-where-you-live.rationale: They reject both state citizenship rights and nationalist emigration schemes, and the sources do not address it.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: They stress action and will, though they analyse capital's restructuring.

ban-cartels.rationale: State action to preserve competition serves capitalism.

no-bailouts.rationale: Opposed to both, since capital and state support each other; indifferent.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: They reject democratic majorities and courts alike.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: They reject official bodies and representation.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: State agreements are rejected as capital's governance.

moral-incentives.rationale: Bonanno rejects sacrifice and duty ethics while favouring joy.

armed-group-creates-revolution.rationale: Propaganda of the deed and small groups meant to spark revolt, though they reject vanguard roles; the 'revolutionary gymnastics' idea is close.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: They want all privilege and power abolished.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: Rule of any kind is rejected.

patriotic-education.rationale: Nationalism and state education are rejected.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: Not addressed; they reject both state preferences and racism.

public-money-creation.rationale: State money is still money and state.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Bonanno stresses its adaptability and restructuring, which is why they favour permanent attack.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Bonanno stresses flexible exploitation, not the aristocracy thesis.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: They condemn racism and property rights.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: State treaties are not their concern.

elective-rulers.rationale: Elections are fictitious and rulers rejected.

minority-veto.rationale: Consensus and individual autonomy in affinity groups mean no binding decisions without consent.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: They support resistance, though to all rulers, not only lawless ones.

parliament-supreme.rationale: Parliamentary decree is an illusory emancipation.

animal-suffering-matters.rationale: Not addressed though the animal liberation milieu overlaps; split.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: Condemnation of sacrifice, charity and hierarchy.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: Permanent conflict and attack are the opposite of withdrawal.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: Bonanno sees courts and culture as spectacle of capital.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Bonanno describes democratic management as domination through participation.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: They describe global capital but not a Dependency thesis.

native-born-offices.rationale: Offices and nationality categories are rejected.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: Autonomy is central but this is a state-level question.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: They oppose fascism but not constitutional values.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: They reject all states, but the equivalence is a liberal claim; split.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: Slavery as cause is the standard historical view and they oppose it.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: Monuments of state and power are targets.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: The sources say nothing about gendered disadvantage programmes, so adherents have no stated position.

domestic-violence-symmetry.rationale: The sources say nothing on this, and state programmes of any kind are not their concern.

paid-care-work.rationale: Wage labour is the target, so they would not wage care.

filial-duty.rationale: Duties and sacrifice morality are rejected.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: Nationalist state economic policy is rejected.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: They reject marital law, so would not demand proof of fault.

recallable-delegates.rationale: They reject representation altogether, but delegates bound and recallable is closer than parliament.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Private finance and state pensions both opposed.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: Parliament is an illusion; they reject budgets and state.

land-use-tenure.rationale: Use over property is anarchist, but not stated here.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: Legal doctrine is of no concern to them.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: State aid to insurgents is state strategy, though they back rebels themselves.

corporate-influence.rationale: They see capital and state as fused.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: State control for sovereignty is nationalist.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local property rules still property and authority; inferred.

job-guarantee.rationale: They reject the work ethic and wage labour.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: Law is capital's mythology and illegalism is just a means.

state-harmful.rationale: Bonanno calls for the complete elimination of all power and the state must be actively ended since it will not disappear on its own.

informal-organisation.rationale: Affinity groups in place of permanent organisations are the signature insurrectionary position; permanent bodies are said to become ends in themselves.

non-intervention.rationale: Insurrectionists reject all states and do not argue about state-to-state rights; they would attack any state rather than defend sovereignty.

industrial-unions.rationale: Insurrectionists reject permanent unions and federations as bureaucratic organs that negotiate within capitalism.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: The tradition is internationalist and opposes nationalism and scapegoating, and nothing in the texts supports conspiracy claims against a minority.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: Insurrectionists reject state law and regulation of relationships; inferred from their anti-state position, as the sources do not mention marriage.

public-access-to-information.rationale: Insurrectionists seek to abolish the state, not to reform it with legal rights, though they favour open circulation of information; adherents are neutral on a legal right.

local-production.rationale: The texts address attack on capitalism rather than the geography of production.

national-law-over-international.rationale: Insurrectionists reject all law and all states, so they would give no precedence to a national constitution; inferred.

religious-nation.rationale: The theses reject organised religion and the nation-state as mechanisms of domination.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: Insurrectionists reject all hierarchy and domination between peoples as well as within them, so ritual submission to a power is contrary to their principles.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Not addressed; they reject the state and fiscal arrangements alike, so neither regional retention nor pooling is a position they would adopt.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Bonanno attacks property in the means of production and the state's property regime; personal belongings are not a target, so mild agreement is inferred.

defeat-communism.rationale: Insurrectionists oppose communism as a state project but fight the capitalist state; they would not support defeating communism as a state aim.

mixed-public-service-providers.rationale: They reject the state and capitalism entirely and refuse institutional mediation, so publicly funded systems run by state or private providers are both rejected.

religion-illusion.rationale: Bonanno and the Notes critique religion as a mechanism of domination; the sources do not give the specific materialist claim, so agreement is inferred.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: Insurrectionists see capitalism as domination to be attacked now, not a stage laying a foundation; the sources do not discuss historical progress.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Anarcha-feminist-friendly anti-capitalism implies that gender subordination is tied to domination structures, but the sources do not address it directly.

socialized-care.rationale: They oppose state-provided services as institutions of domination, so public provision of care is inferred to be rejected; also private family work is not their programme.

purge-loanwords.rationale: They reject state language policy and nationalism as part of the apparatus of domination.

treaties-binding.rationale: Insurrectionists reject state authority and its treaties wholesale, so the question about binding treaties does not fit their framework.

cooperative-communities.rationale: They favour small affinity groups but reject fixed models and blueprints, and the sources do not endorse common-property communities as a programme.

majority-settlement.rationale: They reject state action and nationalism outright, so state-promoted settlement to bind regions to the nation is opposed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: They reject both capitalism and state communism, but refuse to propose a prescribed third system, so the claim of a needed "third course" is mismatched.

missingStatements.text: Organisation for political struggle should consist of small, informal groups of people who know and trust one another, rather than permanent parties, unions or federations.
missingStatements.rationale: Affinity groups in place of permanent organisations are the signature insurrectionary position; permanent bodies are said to become ends in themselves.

missingStatements.text: Those who oppose the existing order should refuse all negotiation, mediation and compromise with those in power.
missingStatements.rationale: Attack is defined as the refusal of mediation, pacification, accommodation and compromise.
missingStatements.declined: Covered by direct-action, means-match-ends and revolution-justified.

missingStatements.text: Illegal action, such as sabotage and property destruction, is a legitimate means of political struggle.
missingStatements.rationale: Sabotage and attack on infrastructure are central, and illegalism is called a means, often a good one.

notes: Adherents split over armed organisations versus purely informal action, and over whether insurrection is a prelude to revolution (sasha k) or already under way (Bonanno). Anarcho-primitivist and nihilist offshoots would answer technology and civilisation items more strongly.
